items.placeName: Sunworld Hòn Thơm - Hon Thom Cable Car Phu Quoc

facebook.caption:
19,455 reviews. 4.5 stars. And most tourists still don't plan enough time here.

Sunworld Hòn Thơm is three things in one: a record-breaking cable car ride over open ocean, an Ancient Rome-themed shopping hub, and a full island water park on the other side.

The cable car alone spans 7,899m. One of the longest non-stop cable car rides in the world. You feel it.

Book a full day. Not a half day. Save this for your Phu Quoc trip.
facebook.video_caption: Cable car. Open ocean. Ancient Rome architecture. Then a water park on an island. Sunworld Hòn Thơm packs more into one day than most people plan for their whole trip. 4.5 stars across 19,455 reviews. That number means something.

facebook.caption: Tourists keep walking past this. Sunset Town in Phu Quoc looks like a European village dropped onto a Vietnamese island. Colorful facades, canal bridges, street performers at dusk. facebook.caption:
4.8 stars. 2,641 reviews. At a beach restaurant most tourists never find.

Camia Restaurant sits right on the sand in Ông Lang, one of Phu Quoc's quieter stretches of coast. Asian fusion done properly. The kind of place that earns repeat visits, not just one viral photo.

Ông Lang is worth the detour alone. Camia is the reason to stay for dinner.

Save this for your Phu Quoc trip.

facebook.caption:
4.9 stars. 841 reviews. On a beach island in Vietnam.

Bombay Indian Restaurant Phú Quốc is pulling numbers most restaurants in any city would kill for. Butter chicken, dal makhani, fresh naan. Real north Indian cooking, not watered-down tourist food.

Dinner for two lands around $30. That's it.

If you're craving something that isn't seafood or pho, this is the move. Save this for your Phu Quoc trip.

4.7 stars across 246 reviews. That's consistency, not luck.
